narrative:
The model estimates there’s a 41% chance you won’t pass your final year, which is well above the 10% threshold that requires extra support. Because of this, you’ll need to take remedial courses to help you stay on track.

The main reasons the model is concerned come down to three key areas. First, you’ve never failed a class before, which actually works in your favor—it shows you have a solid foundation. However, the other two factors are pulling the prediction in the opposite direction. Unlike most of your classmates, you don’t plan to pursue higher education, which the model sees as a red flag for motivation. Additionally, your long commute to school—30 to 60 minutes each way—may be making it harder to balance your time and energy for studying.

Other details in your profile also played a role, though less strongly. For example, your parents’ education levels are lower than average, and you don’t have internet access at home, which could limit your resources. You also spend a lot of free time socializing and going out, which might be cutting into study hours. On the positive side, your family relationships are strong, and you’ve attended nursery school, both of which support your learning.

The remedial courses will give you extra time to focus on your studies, especially in areas where you might be struggling. It’s also a good idea to think about how you can use your time more effectively—maybe adjusting your schedule to reduce distractions or finding ways to study even without internet. This is a chance to build habits that will help you succeed.
